title: Python: encrypt + decrypt
close_reason: Completed Python OSCORE encrypt+decrypt validation through the real MemorySecurityContext.protect()/unprotect() API against RFC 8613 Appendix C published vectors in test/vectors/oscore.json: request protection C.4-C.6 byte-exact (OSCORE option + ciphertext), full response exchange C.7 (nonce reuse) and C.8 (fresh PIV) including client-side decrypt of published ciphertexts, real protect->unprotect roundtrips with replay rejection, PIV wire encoding at boundaries 0/255/256/2^40-1, nonce XOR construction at boundaries, and decrypt-path rejection of short ciphertexts. Fixed a protocol gap: unprotect() now rejects PIVs >5 bytes per RFC 8613 Section 5.2 (aiocoap accepts up to 7; vector piv_overflow_rejected). Corrected one corrupt nibble in test/vectors/oscore.json piv_boundary_nonce_xor_max expected nonce (...110aab6783 -> ...1104ab6783): the old value was never consumed by any implementation and contradicts RFC 8613 Figure-5 arithmetic (0xfb^0xff=0x04) as confirmed by the four passing RFC-published nonces; rust/lichen-oscore vectors still pass 10/10. Validation: tests/crypto/test_oscore_vectors.py 38 passed (was 23); tests/crypto 379 passed; ruff check+format clean; mypy no new errors. Full suite: 8844 passed; the 13 failures (edhoc_responder restart, sos_resource, rpl dao, ipv6 srh hop-limit, edhoc generator drift, ccp9 rendezvous) were A/B-verified as pre-existing by rerunning them with the new PIV check disabled - identical results.
